content.definition: Complementary foods are foods given in addition to breast milk after 6 months of age to provide additional nutrients and energy for growth and brain development.
content.breastfeeding_continuation: Breast milk should be continued together with complementary food for 2 years and beyond.
content.philosophy: Proper nutrition in early childhood is an investment in a successful, intelligent, and healthy future.

content.hygiene_protocol: Wash hands before preparing baby's food and before feeding. Use a separate plate/bowl and spoon for the baby.
content.environment: Feed in a designated place with minimum distraction. Do not feed while the baby is walking around or watching television.
content.restrictions: Do not add salt or sugar to food until 1 year of age.
content.interaction: Talk to the baby lovingly with eye-to-eye contact; allow the baby to eat slowly and be patient.

content.day_01_protocol: Prepare food in a semi-solid soft form using very well-mashed rice. Mix with expressed breast milk for familiarity. Give 2-3 tea spoons.
content.day_02_to_03_protocol: Give one or two meals a day of very well-mashed rice. Gradually increase the amount at each meal while breastfeeding on demand.

content.meal_composition: Add pulses (e.g., dhal) to the rice. Introduce one new food at a time for 2-3 days before adding another.
content.amount: 3-4 tea spoons at a time, twice a day.
content.fruit: Give a tea spoon of well-mashed fruit (e.g., papaya, banana) after the rice meal.

content.animal_protein: Introduce powdered dried sprats, fish, or chicken to the rice/dhal mix. Animal foods are rich in iron for brain development.
content.sprat_preparation: Wash sprats whole, air or oven dry/roast, then grind whole into a fine texture. Add one tea spoon per meal.
content.energy_boost: Temper with 1-2 tea spoons of oil/butter or cook with thick coconut milk.

content.meal_composition: Mashed rice + pulse (green gram/gram) + animal food (fish/meat/liver) + yellow vegetables (pumpkin/carrot/sweet potato).
content.amount: 5-6 tea spoons at a time, twice a day.
content.fruit_snack: 1-2 tea spoons of mashed banana or papaya between or after main meals.

content.green_leaves: Introduce local greens: Gotukola, Drumstick leaves (Murunga), Sarana, Thampala, or Mukunuwenna.
content.meal_rotation: Vary items daily (e.g., Gotukola for lunch, Sarana for dinner) for brain development.
content.serving_size: About 1/4 of a tea cup, 2-3 times a day.
content.hydration: Offer sips of boiled, cooled water after meals.

content.texture_change: Transition to coarsely mashed rice with pulses, iron-rich animal foods, and vegetables.
content.portion: 1/2 tea cup at a time, 2-3 times a day.
content.snack: Well-mashed fruit, 2-3 tea spoons, 1-2 times a day.
content.doctor_advice_note: If complementary food was started before 6 months on medical advice, continue this pattern until 7 months.

content.meal_composition: Coarsely mashed rice with pulses, animal food, eggs, and green leaves.
content.diversity_rationale: Various food types increase nutrient availability, allow the child to learn different tastes, and develop lifelong healthy eating habits.
content.snacks: 1-2 snacks a day between main meals.

content.meal_spec: Half a tea cup of coarsely chopped food, 2-3 times a day. 4-5 tea spoons of scraped fruit after meals.
content.cognitive_interaction: During meals: 1. Point out and name foods. 2. Show different colors. 3. Talk about different tastes.
content.benefit: Active engagement during meal times stimulates learning and brain development.

content.sprat_processing: Wash sprats whole without removing the head[cite: 1107]. Air or oven dry/roast and grind into a fine texture[cite: 1056, 1107].
content.dosage: Add approximately one tea spoon of powdered sprats to a prepared meal[cite: 1056].
content.rationale: Animal foods are rich in iron and essential for brain development, which is fastest in the first 2 years[cite: 1015, 1056].

content.fat_additives: Temper food with 1-2 tea spoons of oil or butter[cite: 1053, 1078].
content.local_alternative: Cook food with thick coconut milk to increase energy content[cite: 1078].
content.purpose: Increasing energy density is vital for growing infants with small stomach capacities[cite: 1059].

content.standard_mix: Half mashed rice combined with a pulse (dhal/green gram) and animal food (fish/chicken/liver)[cite: 1056].
content.vegetable_additions: Include yellow vegetables like pumpkin, carrot, or yellow sweet potatoes[cite: 1056].
content.serving_amount: 5-6 tea spoons per meal, given twice daily[cite: 1056].

content.greens_list: Introduce Gotukola, drumstick leaves (Murunga), Sarana, Thampala, or Mukunuwenna[cite: 1069].
content.rotation_rule: Give different food items at different meals (e.g., Gotukola for lunch, Sarana for dinner)[cite: 1062].
content.serving_size: About 1/4 of a tea cup, 2-3 times per day[cite: 1056].

content.milestone: By completion of 7 months, transition from well-mashed to coarsely mashed rice[cite: 1114].
content.composition: Mix coarsely mashed rice with pulses, iron-rich animal origin foods, and vegetables[cite: 1056].
content.hydration: Offer sips of boiled, cooled water after main meals[cite: 1057].

content.ebm_room_temp: Expressed Breast Milk (EBM) is safe at room temperature for up to 8 hours[cite: 1042].
content.ebm_refrigeration: EBM can be stored in a refrigerator for 24 hours[cite: 1042].
content.ebm_freezer: EBM remains safe in a freezer compartment for up to 3 months[cite: 1042].

content.meal_frequency: Main meal given 2-3 times a day, consisting of half a tea cup of food[cite: 1056].
content.snack_frequency: 1-2 snacks per day between main meals[cite: 1056, 1091].
content.learning_phase: This is a special period where the child learns to accept various foods and different tastes[cite: 1022, 1097].

content.education_during_meals: Point out different foods and name them to the baby[cite: 1100].
content.visual_stimulation: Show the baby the different colors present in their meal[cite: 1100].
content.sensory_learning: Talk about the different tastes of the food[cite: 1100].

content.maternal_vitamin_a: Postpartum mothers should receive 200,000 IU of Vitamin A before hospital discharge or within 2 weeks of delivery[cite: 1127].
content.infant_vitamin_a_9mo: 100,000 IU Mega dose is given at 9 months alongside the measles vaccine[cite: 1123].
content.infant_vitamin_a_18mo: 100,000 IU Mega dose is given at 18 months with the 4th dose of OPV/DPT/Hep.B[cite: 1123].

content.weighing_schedule: Children under 24 months should be weighed monthly[cite: 1148].
content.clinic_protocol: Children up to 6 months should be weighed at clinics[cite: 1150].
content.field_protocol: Children after 6 months should be weighed at field weighing posts[cite: 1150].

content.prevalence: Nearly 30% of children under five in Sri Lanka suffer from iron deficiency anaemia[cite: 1013].
content.consequences: Iron deficiency leads to reduced IQ and impaired national development[cite: 1017].
content.intervention: Include iron-rich animal foods like liver and sprats daily from the 7th month[cite: 1067, 1068].

content.rule_of_introduction: Introduce only one new food item at a time[cite: 1062].
content.observation_period: Continue the same new food for 3-4 days before introducing the next to monitor for reactions[cite: 1062].
content.symptoms: Watch for excessive crying, urticaria (hives), vomiting, colics, diarrhoea, or wheezing[cite: 1065].

content.plant_sources: Iron-rich local plants include Gotukola, Sarana, Thampala, and green gram[cite: 1069].
content.absorption_hack: Include Vitamin C sources (lemon, lime, guava, papaya) in the same meal to increase iron absorption[cite: 1070].
content.preparation_hack: Soak, germinate, or ferment pulses to improve iron bioavailability[cite: 1071].

content.texture_requirement: Food should be coarsely chopped or mashed[cite: 1056, 1114].
content.self_feeding: Introduce 'finger foods' the baby can pick up, such as pieces of bread or hoppers[cite: 1094, 1115].
content.frequency: 3-4 meals plus breast feeds, with 1-2 snacks depending on appetite[cite: 1056, 1091].

content.yolk_timing: Introduce egg yolk from the 7th month[cite: 1076].
content.white_timing: Introduce egg white from the 9th month[cite: 1077].
content.preparation: Eggs must be well-cooked (boiled or fried until firm)[cite: 1076].

content.main_diet: By 12 months, the child should be eating family foods (chopped/coarsely mashed)[cite: 1118].
content.breastfeeding_position: Breast milk should be given after main meals, not as a replacement[cite: 1045, 1046].

content.eligibility: Thriposha is provided to infants with growth faltering or underweight from 6 months to one year[cite: 1121].
content.maternal_use: Breastfeeding mothers should receive Thriposha for a minimum of six months[cite: 1126].

content.during_illness: Continue breastfeeding and offer small, energy-dense meals frequently[cite: 1138, 1144].
content.recovery_phase: Give one extra meal daily for at least 2 weeks after the illness has passed[cite: 1139].
content.hydration: Increase fluid intake during bouts of illness[cite: 1141].

content.self_feeding_goal: Children should be able to feed themselves without assistance by age two[cite: 1096].
content.forced_feeding: Forced feeding is discouraged at all times; caregivers should be sensitive to hunger and satiety cues[cite: 1098].
content.sensory_exploration: Allow children to touch food with hands, provided hands are washed with soap first[cite: 1099].

content.standard_volume: A standard Sri Lankan 'tea cup' for measurement is defined as 200 ml[cite: 1056, 1204].
content.rice_serving: 1/2 a tea cup of cooked rice equals one serving[cite: 1182].
content.bread_serving: One slice of bread (from a 450g loaf cut into 9 slices) equals one serving[cite: 1183].

content.wasting_stats: Wasting in Sri Lankan children under five has remained stagnant at 14% for a long period[cite: 1012].
content.underweight_stats: 29.4% of children under five are classified as underweight[cite: 1011].
content.stunting_stats: 13.5% of children in this age group are stunted[cite: 1011].

content.optimal_start: Introduce complementary foods immediately upon the completion of 180 days (6 months)[cite: 1025, 1027].
content.early_start_limit: Never introduce complementary foods before 120 days (4 months) as it is physiologically harmful[cite: 1036].
content.delayed_start_risk: Delaying beyond 6 months adversely impacts growth and the ability to consume family foods at one year[cite: 1037].

content.working_mothers: Employed mothers are encouraged to express breast milk (EBM)[cite: 1041].
content.feeding_tool: EBM should be fed using a clean cup or a cup and a tea spoon[cite: 1043].
content.bottle_warning: Avoid using feeding bottles to prevent hygiene issues and nipple confusion[cite: 1110].

content.oil_quantity: Add 1-2 tea spoons of oil to food to increase energy density[cite: 1053].
content.consistency: Introduce foods in thick form rather than watery/thin form to ensure more nutrients per volume[cite: 1048].
content.appetite: The appropriate number of meals depends on the energy density of the food and the amount consumed[cite: 1051, 1052].

content.daily_energy_target: 200 kcal per day from complementary foods[cite: 1056].
content.meal_amount: Increase gradually from 2-3 spoonfuls to a little more than 1/2 a tea cup per meal[cite: 1056].
content.snack_option: Offer 1-2 snacks depending on the child's appetite[cite: 1056].

content.form: Fruits should be given in mashed or pulped form, not as juices[cite: 1073].
content.citrus: When giving orange or mandarin, a minimal amount of water can be added[cite: 1074].
content.frequency: Locally available fruits should be included in the daily diet[cite: 1073].

content.dairy_snacks: Milk-based products like yogurt and curd can be introduced from the 7th month[cite: 1082].
content.curd_serving: Curd should be served without adding sugar or honey[cite: 1083].
content.benefit: Locally available, low-cost nutritious foods are preferred over processed packet foods[cite: 1084].

content.interventions: If growth faltering occurs, introduce energy-rich snacks like bread with butter/margarine[cite: 1088].
content.extra_meals: Increase the amount fed at a time or add an extra meal to the daily routine[cite: 1088].
content.fat_boost: Increase energy density by adding a source of fat (oil/butter) to every meal[cite: 1088].

content.general_dosage: 2mg per kg of body weight per day of elemental iron[cite: 1129].
content.community_dosage: 12.5mg of elemental iron daily for 2 months[cite: 1130].
content.preterm_lbw: Babies born preterm or with low birth weight (LBW) must receive iron supplements from 2 months onwards[cite: 1131, 1132].

content.length_checks: Length must be measured at 4, 9, and 18 months[cite: 1152].
content.height_checks: After age two, measure height every 6 months[cite: 1152].
content.stunting_risk: If at risk of stunting, measure length every 2 months up to age two[cite: 1153].

content.definition: A snack is a small quantity of energy-dense food or drink taken between main meals[cite: 1175].
content.local_examples: Traditional snacks like Helapa, sago pudding, or Aggala can be given after one year[cite: 1178].
content.quick_options: Boiled gram, green gram, or boiled potatoes with scraped coconut[cite: 1177].

content.protein_weight: 25-50g of cooked fish/chicken/meat equals one serving[cite: 1199].
content.visual_aid: A serving of meat/fish is roughly the size of a matchbox[cite: 1199].
content.sprats: 6 sprats are considered equivalent to one serving of meat/fish[cite: 1199].

content.cooked_veg: 3 tablespoons of cooked fruit-vegetables (e.g., pumpkin) equals one serving[cite: 1202].
content.leafy_greens: 1/2 a tea cup of cooked leafy vegetables equals one serving[cite: 1203].

content.liquid_milk: 100 ml of milk equals one serving[cite: 1190].
content.powdered_milk: 3 heaped tea spoons of milk powder equal one serving[cite: 1193].
content.cheese: A piece of cheese the size of a small matchbox equals one serving[cite: 1192].

content.supplement_package: Postpartum mothers need Iron, folic acid, Vitamin C, and Calcium for at least 6 months[cite: 1126].
content.maternal_nutrition: Mothers should be supported to eat well to sustain successful breastfeeding[cite: 1126].

content.nutritional_need: Breast milk alone is insufficient for the rapidly growing child after 6 months[cite: 1021].
content.munching_skill: Introduction of foods helps teach the baby to munch, aiding transition to family foods[cite: 1022].
content.long_term_health: Early nutrition in the first two years determines health in adulthood[cite: 1014, 1016].

content.utensil_rule: Use clean utensils for preparation and do not use them for other purposes[cite: 1109].
content.hand_washing: Caregivers must wash hands with soap and water before preparation and feeding[cite: 1107].

content.fat_source: 1-2 teaspoons of coconut oil can be used per meal[cite: 1078].
content.margarine: 1-2 teaspoons of margarine or butter can be added to cooked food[cite: 1078].
content.palatability: Adding fat makes food softer and more palatable for infants[cite: 1080].

content.posture_change: An awake baby's posture should be changed at least once every half hour[cite: 821, 836].
content.interaction: The baby should be cuddled and talked to lovingly to promote emotional well-being[cite: 822].

content.risk_foods: Avoid small, rounded, hard pieces of vegetables and whole nuts/pulses[cite: 1086].
content.supervision: Always be vigilant when the baby is consuming 'finger foods' to prevent choking[cite: 1115].

content.definition: Complementary foods are items given in addition to breast milk after 6 months of age because breast milk alone is no longer sufficient for a rapidly growing child[cite: 1009].
content.purpose: They provide additional nutrients and energy required for optimal growth, brain development, and overall health[cite: 1009].

content.duration: While complementary foods are introduced at 6 months, breast milk should continue to be given together with food for 2 years and beyond[cite: 1009].

content.hand_washing: Caregivers must wash hands with soap before preparing baby's food and before feeding the baby[cite: 1010].
content.utensils: The baby should have a dedicated separate plate, bowl, and spoon[cite: 1010].

content.designated_place: Feed the baby in a consistent, designated place with minimum distractions[cite: 1010].
content.screen_time_warning: Do not feed the baby while they are watching television or walking around the house/garden[cite: 1010].

content.interaction: Talk to the baby lovingly with eye-to-eye contact during meals to encourage eating and stimulate brain development[cite: 1010].
content.patience: Caregivers must be patient and allow the baby to eat slowly[cite: 1010].

content.additives: Do not add salt or sugar to the baby's food until they reach 1 year of age[cite: 1010].

content.start_date: Complementary feeding should begin immediately upon the completion of 6 months[cite: 1011].

content.texture: On Day 01, prepare complementary food in a semi-solid soft form[cite: 1011].
content.recipe: Mash rice very well and mix it with expressed breast milk to make the taste familiar[cite: 1011].
content.amount: Give 2-3 tea spoons of this preparation on the first day[cite: 1011].

content.frequency: Give one or two meals a day consisting of very well mashed rice[cite: 1011].
content.breastfeeding: Continue breastfeeding on demand alongside these early meals[cite: 1011].

content.new_foods: Start adding other foods like pulses (e.g., dhal)[cite: 1012].
content.rule: Introduce one new food at a time to the rice for 2-3 days continuously before adding another new item[cite: 1012].
content.amount: Give 3-4 tea spoons at a time, twice a day[cite: 1012].

content.fruit_type: Introduce a tea spoon of well mashed fruit, such as papaya or banana, after the rice meal[cite: 1012].

content.animal_source: Adding animal origin food like powdered dried sprats, fish, or chicken to the rice/dhal mix is very important[cite: 1013].
content.rationale: Animal foods are rich in iron and help brain development, which is fastest in the first 2 years of life[cite: 1013].

content.sprat_processing: Wash sprats without removing the head, then air/oven dry or roast them[cite: 1013].
content.grinding: Grind them whole to a fine texture and store in a bottle[cite: 1013].
content.dosage: Add about one tea spoon when preparing a meal[cite: 1013].

content.additives: Temper food with 1-2 tea spoons of oil or butter, or cook with thick coconut milk to increase energy content[cite: 1013].

content.recipe: Use half mashed rice mixed with a pulse (dhal, green gram), animal food (fish, chicken, meat, liver, sprats), and vegetables (pumpkin, carrot, yellow sweet potatoes)[cite: 1014].
content.portion: Give 5-6 tea spoons at a time, twice a day[cite: 1014].

content.snack: Give 1-2 tea spoons of well mashed banana or papaw in between or after main meals[cite: 1014].

content.greens_list: Include gotukola, drumstick leaves (murunga kola), sarana, thampala, or mukunuwenna with mashed rice[cite: 1015].
content.rotation: Try giving different food items at different meals (e.g., gotukola for lunch, sarana for dinner) for better growth[cite: 1015].

content.amount: Give about 1/4 of a tea cup at a time, 2-3 times a day[cite: 1015].
content.water: Offer sips of boiled, cooled water to the baby after meals[cite: 1015].

content.texture_change: By completion of 7 months, move to coarsely mashed rice[cite: 1016].
content.portion: Give 1/2 tea cup at a time, 2-3 times a day[cite: 1016].
content.fruit_portion: Give 2-3 tea spoons of well mashed fruit 1-2 times a day[cite: 1016].

content.meal_mix: Coarsely mashed rice with pulses (dhal, germinated green gram, soya), iron-rich animal food, eggs, vegetables, and green leaves[cite: 1017].
content.rationale: Various food types ensure the child gets required nutrients and learns different tastes to develop healthy eating habits[cite: 1017].

content.educational_feeding: During meals, point out different foods and name them, show different colours, and talk about different tastes[cite: 1008].
content.benefit: This actively helps learning and brain development[cite: 1008].

content.main_meals: Introduce variety like Jak and breadfruit[cite: 1019].
content.portion: Give a bit more than 1/2 tea cup at a time, 2-3 times a day[cite: 1019].

content.finger_foods: Provide small pieces of hopper (soft center), bread with butter, or ripe avocado[cite: 1019].
content.safety_warning: Important: Do not leave the baby alone with finger foods. Caregivers must help and encourage self-feeding[cite: 1019].

content.frequency: Give a bit more than 1/2 tea cup of coarsely chopped food, 3-4 times a day[cite: 1020].
content.social_feeding: Try to let the baby sit with family members during meal times[cite: 1020].

content.presentation: Rice and 'curries' can be served separately and mixed while feeding[cite: 1021].
content.portion: Give 3/4 tea cup of food at a time, 3-4 times a day[cite: 1021].

content.diet_type: The baby should be eating nutritious family foods now[cite: 1022].
content.portion: A bit more than a tea cup at each meal, 3 times a day[cite: 1022].
content.diversity: Try to feed 5 different items of vegetables and fruits per day[cite: 1022].

content.cereals: Rice, Milk rice, string hoppers, hoppers, thosai etc.: 2 cups for the whole day.

content.pulses: Cooked dhal, green gram, cowpea: 3 - 6 Table spoons for the whole day.

content.vegetables: Different types of vegetables: 3 - 6 Table spoons for the whole day.
content.leafy_greens: Green leaves: Half of a tea cup for the whole day.

content.meat_fish: Fish/chicken/meat/liver: Two pieces the size of a match-box.

content.cheese: A piece the size of a match box.

content.fruit_portions: Give fruits twice a day (e.g., one medium size banana, one orange).

content.definition: Snacks are nutritious foods, taken in small amounts, which are rich in energy and nutrients[cite: 1024].
content.purpose: They give extra energy and nutrients in a small amount of food.

content.potato_snack: A small nutritious snack like a piece of boiled potato with a bit of butter added.
content.egg_snack: A piece of boiled egg can be used as a snack.

content.introduction: Start feeding eggs 2 weeks after starting complementary food.
content.sequence: Feed a little bit of boiled egg yolk first. Start the boiled white component about one week later.
content.benefits: Eggs are a less expensive nutritious food that can be given daily.

content.patience: Feed an ill child very patiently in small amounts frequently[cite: 1018].
content.recovery_protocol: During recovery, give an extra meal and extra breastfeeds for about 2 weeks after recovery from illness[cite: 1018].

content.frequency: Weigh the child every month until the 2nd birthday[cite: 1026].
content.length_checks: Length should be checked at least at 4, 9, 12, and 18 months[cite: 1026].
content.documentation: Ensure all growth measurements are marked in the Child Health Development Record (CHDR)[cite: 1026].

content.special_advice: If the child is overweight, underweight, or has growth faltering, seek special nutritional advice from healthcare staff[cite: 1027].

content.restriction: Formula milk should not be encouraged. Its introduction should only be decided by a doctor[cite: 1027].
content.risk: Formula milk in the 1st year could have adverse long-term health effects[cite: 1027].

content.chdr_resource: Parents should read the yellow pages in the CHDR[cite: 1027].
content.contact: Ask your Public Health Midwife or doctor to explain anything you do not understand[cite: 1027].

content.visual_portion: For a 1-2 year old, meat/fish portions are visually approximated as 'match-box-size' pieces.

content.kunissan: Small shrimp (Kunissan) daily requirement is 2 table spoons.

content.hopper_prep: When giving hoppers as finger food, use only the soft center portion[cite: 1019].

content.frequency_logic: Give 1-2 snacks a day depending on the baby's weight gain and hunger cues.

content.symptom_management: Manage/control symptoms such as fever before offering food, as a feverish child will refuse food[cite: 1018].

content.additives_illness: During illness, add oil and thick coconut milk to food as usual to maintain energy intake[cite: 1018].

content.amount: Give a bit more than 1/2 tea cup of food at a time for main meals[cite: 1020].

content.sequence: Breastfeeding can follow a meal[cite: 1015]. At 9-11 months, breastfeed after meals[cite: 1021].

content.fruit_amount: Give scraped fruit about 1/4 tea cup in between or after main meals[cite: 1019].
Give about 4 teaspoons of well mashed fruit after main meals or as a snack[cite: 1017].
